title: Constancy conjecture for cyclic solutions of the functional equations
statement:
Let $s\geq1$, let $0\leq\gamma<s$, and let ${\mathcal A}_{\gamma}$ be the analytic-function algebra considered in the source. Let $\mathcal S$ be the multiplicative semigroup generated by the integers $N_1,\ldots,N_s$, and let $g\in{\mathcal A}_{\gamma}$ be cyclic. Assume that, for every $N\in\mathcal S$, $g$ satisfies

$$
g((z^N)^N)=\prod_{\zeta^N=1}g(\zeta z).
$$

**Constancy conjecture.** Then $g$ is constant. The source presents this as a proposed extension of the assertion that non-constant outer solutions do not occur in the corresponding class; it does not provide a proof or a resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.6416

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).
source_name: Christopher Deninger, “Invariant measures on the circle and functional equations”, arXiv:1111.6416 (2011).
